# FPML -> CDM Cookbook: fx-derivatives

## Status

- Operational status: ready
- Agent use policy: Agents may apply these rules during normal FPML to CDM proposal generation.
- Semantic success rate: 100%
- Draft quality: strong
- Draft publication: success

## Trigger Signals

Apply this page when the FpML document includes any of the following top-level sections or product cues:
- fx-derivatives
- FpML sections: header, party, trade
- Trade substructures commonly observed:
  - trade > fxSingleLeg
  - trade > tradeHeader
- Party identifiers and references:
  - party > partyId
  - tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId
- Header metadata:
  - header > conversationId, creationTimestamp, messageId, sendTo, sentBy

## Canonical Mapping Procedure

1. Start from the repeated FpML sections: header, party, trade. [Ensure these sections are present before applying downstream rules.]
2. Map trade identifiers, party references, and trade dates before product-specific economics.
3. Apply recurring mapping rules only when the exact source cues appear in the document (see Stable Rules and Transformations).
4. Apply non-literal transformations (normalizations/reshaping) where indicated by the evidence below.
5. Assemble under CDM scaffolding such as meta and trade, preserving traceability to source identifiers.
6. Treat generated identifiers, global keys, and unmatched party identifiers as enrichments unless the source proves otherwise.

## Stable Rules

- Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
  - When it applies: FpML contains tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId elements.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value.
  - Validate: Verify all FpML tradeId values are preserved in CDM assignedIdentifier.identifier.value. Check for unexpected duplication or scheme differences and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: tradeId is absent in FpML.
  - Exceptions/notes: Some CDM outputs contain more identifiers than FpML tradeId elements; scheme may differ. Trigger human review in those cases.

- Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate includes a trailing 'Z' (UTC designator).
  - Inspect: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeDate.value (plain ISO date without trailing 'Z').
  - Validate: Confirm only the trailing 'Z' was trimmed; no timezone semantics needed elsewhere.
  - Do not apply when: FpML tradeDate is already a plain date without timezone.

- Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
  - When it applies: FpML includes trade.fxdigitaloption.productType strings.
  - Inspect: trade.fxdigitaloption.productType (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (normalized taxonomy string).
  - Validate: Confirm productType string normalized as observed in evidence; flag if normalization logic is unclear or out of scope.
  - Do not apply when: No productType present.
  - Exceptions/notes: Normalization details are not exhaustively specified; may require analyst review.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: FpML provides expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime and a businessCenter.
  - Inspect: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and related businessCenter fields (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value and exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime and expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: Confirm date, time, and business center are correctly placed. Ensure no timezone semantics are dropped.
  - Do not apply when: Any of expiry date, time, or business center is missing; mark partials for review.

- Payment amounts -> CDM quantities (value + currency unit)
  - When it applies: FpML includes exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Inspect: exchangedCurrency1.paymentAmount and exchangedCurrency2.paymentAmount (amount, currency) (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and trade.tradeLot.quantity.unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm amount and currency are preserved, including sign/scale. If multiple paymentAmount or splitSettlement entries exist, verify any aggregation logic and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: paymentAmount is absent.

## Transformations

- Resolve party hrefs -> CDM party references and roles
  - When it applies: FpML contains partyReference hrefs and buyer/seller or payer/receiver references.
  - Inspect: partyReference hrefs in buyer/seller and payer/receiver contexts (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: party references with roles (e.g., Party1/Party2) used in buyerSeller and payout sections.
  - Validate: Cross-check Party1/Party2 and payer/receiver with FpML references; flag any polarity inversions for analyst review.
  - Do not apply when: partyReference hrefs are missing or ambiguous.
  - Exceptions/notes: Evidence shows possible inversions of roles; treat polarity as tentative and review-critical.

- Date normalization (trim trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML tradeHeader.tradeDate includes 'Z'.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.tradeDate.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradedate.value without 'Z'.
  - Validate: Only the trailing 'Z' is removed; no timezone conversion implied.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter present in FpML.
  - Inspect: expirydatetime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter.
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value; exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime; expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: All three components preserved.

- PaymentAmount -> Quantity mapping
  - When it applies: exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount fields present.
  - Inspect: paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Preserve amount, currency, sign, and scale. For multiple entries, confirm aggregation or separate entries per evidence and flag if unclear.

- ExchangeRate + quoted pair -> Price assembly
  - When it applies: FpML has exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2.
  - Inspect: fxSingleLeg.exchangeRate.rate; exchangeRate.quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2; any quoteBasis context if present.
  - Propose CDM: price.value.value, price.unit.currency.value, price.perUnitOf.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm price numeric value and currency unit/perUnitOf assigned per the quotedCurrencyPair; flag if quoteBasis/strikeQuoteBasis interpretation is needed and not explicit.
  - Do not apply when: exchangeRate or quotedCurrencyPair is missing.

- Split/Multiple settlement entries -> aggregated quantity
  - When it applies: FpML uses splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries.
  - Inspect: splitSettlement blocks and repeated paymentAmount entries.
  - Propose CDM: either a single aggregated trade.tradeLot.quantity or an appropriate set of aggregated quantities per evidence.
  - Validate: Confirm aggregation approach (sums, ordering, rounding) is consistent with evidence or business rules; otherwise flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: Only a single settlement entry exists.

- Tentative: Normalize trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate -> trade.tradeDate.value
  - Apply only when exact match to the observed pattern; mark for analyst review.

## Variants And Branches

- AssignedIdentifier.scheme differences
  - Signal: Scheme in CDM may differ from FpML tradeIdScheme (or absence thereof).
  - Action: Do not copy scheme verbatim; treat as potential normalization/override. Flag for analyst review.

- Buyer/Seller role inversion
  - Signal: CDM buyer/seller or payer/receiver roles may appear inverted relative to FpML hrefs.
  - Action: Treat role polarity as tentative; require analyst validation of Party1/Party2 mapping.

- Duplicated tradeIdentifier entries
  - Signal: CDM may contain more tradeIdentifier entries than FpML tradeId elements.
  - Action: Do not assume 1:1 mapping; flag duplicates/additional identifiers for review.

## Enrichment And Defaults

- Generated/default party identifiers under partyid.identifier.value
  - Signal: CDM often includes LEI-like or generated party identifiers not present in FpML.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; do not generate unless approved. Flag for review.

- Party LEI or generated identifiers inserted
  - Signal: LEI-like identifiers appear in CDM without FpML source.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; confirm source/approval before populating.

- Metadata taxonomy scheme enrichment under name.meta.scheme
  - Signal: CDM includes taxonomy scheme metadata even when FpML lacks a scheme.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; do not insert without approved default. Flag for review.

- Product type normalization -> taxonomy name and meta.scheme enrichment
  - Signal: Normalized product names and added taxonomy scheme metadata observed.
  - Action: Treat scheme insertion as enrichment; normalization should be limited to evidence-backed patterns; flag for review.

- Taxonomy scheme metadata added under name.meta.scheme
  - Signal: Scheme metadata present in CDM without explicit FpML value.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; verify choice of scheme externally.

## Human Review Triggers

- Source for any LEI or generated party identifiers is absent in FpML; confirm provenance before including.
- Buyer/seller or payer/receiver polarity appears inverted relative to FpML hrefs.
- Unclear derivation of CDM Party1/Party2 labels from FpML party references.
- Duplicated or augmented tradeIdentifier entries relative to FpML tradeId.
- Multiple splitSettlement/paymentAmount entries: confirm aggregation vs separation.
- Differences in assignedIdentifier.scheme vs FpML tradeId scheme: confirm normalization.
- Mapping of exchangedCurrency leg to SettlementPayout payerReceiver is unclear.
- Any tentative pattern applied (date normalization; expiry mapping; price assembly) without explicit cues.

## Validation Checklist

- Identify FpML tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId and confirm CDM trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value preserves each value.
- Check tradeHeader.tradeDate for trailing 'Z'; ensure CDM trade.tradeDate.value trims 'Z'.
- For options, confirm trade.fxdigitaloption.productType is mapped to trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value with expected normalization.
- Confirm expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and businessCenter map to adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value, exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime, and expirationTime.businessCenter.value respectively.
- Verify exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency map to trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value; preserve amount, currency, sign, and scale.
- Resolve partyReference hrefs; verify Party1/Party2 and payer/receiver direction against FpML context.
- When exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2 exist, assemble CDM price.value.value, price.unit.currency.value, price.perUnitOf.currency.value; confirm any quoteBasis interpretation or flag for review.
- If splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries exist, validate aggregation or separation per evidence; flag if logic is unclear.
- Confirm every enriched/defaulted CDM value is either present in FpML or explicitly approved as a default.
- Ensure each populated CDM field in the proposal cites an applicable cookbook rule id or is marked as an assumption.

## Do Not Assume

- Do not treat Generated/default party identifiers appear under partyid.identifier.value as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Party LEI or generated identifiers inserted as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Metadata taxonomy scheme enrichment under name.meta.scheme as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Product type normalization -> taxonomy name and meta.scheme enrichment as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Taxonomy scheme metadata added under name.meta.scheme as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Source of party LEI values missing in FpML.
- Do not infer Party1/Party2, buyer/seller, or payer/receiver direction from document order alone.
- Do not invent identifiers, global keys, external keys, or LEIs when they are not source-backed.
- Do not guess normalized exchange, taxonomy, or scheme values without a controlled mapping or evidence.
- Do not apply tentative patterns without matching source evidence.
- Do not invent enriched identifiers, global keys, exchange codes, or defaults without source-backed evidence.
- Do not treat caveated or unclear behavior as a stable mapping rule.
- Do not treat as stable: Derivation of CDM party role labels (Party1/Party2) from FpML party hrefs.
- Do not treat as stable: Source and reliability of party LEI or generated identifiers included in CDM.
- Do not treat as stable: Rules that create additional or duplicate tradeIdentifier entries in CDM.
- Do not treat as stable: Precise aggregation rules used when merging splitSettlement/multiple paymentAmount entries.

## Worked Examples

- fx-derivatives/fx-ex01-fx-spot.xml -> fx-derivatives/fx-ex01-fx-spot.json
  - Signals: header, trade, party.
  - Guidance: exchange rate copied; payment amounts to quantities; tradeIds copied; strip trailing 'Z' from dates.
  - Validate: Review party LEI source; verify payer/receiver roles.

- fx-derivatives/fx-ex02-spot-cross-w-side-rates.xml -> fx-derivatives/fx-ex02-spot-cross-w-side-rates.json
  - Signals: header, trade, party.
  - Guidance: tradeId -> assignedIdentifier; exchangedCurrency1 amount/currency -> quantity; exchangeRate + quoted pair -> price unit/perUnitOf; resolve hrefs to payer/receiver.
  - Validate: Investigate CDM 'Party1' vs FpML 'party2'; confirm any LEI sources.

- fx-derivatives/fx-ex03-fx-fwd.xml -> fx-derivatives/fx-ex03-fx-fwd.json
  - Signals: header, trade, party.
  - Guidance: tradeId -> assignedIdentifier; payment amounts -> quantities; rate -> price; strip trailing 'Z'.
  - Validate: Check payer/receiver polarity; check for duplicated identifiers.

## Source Evidence

- Quality and publication status: fx-derivatives:QUALITY
- Stable rules: fx-derivatives:RULE-001, fx-derivatives:RULE-002, fx-derivatives:RULE-003, fx-derivatives:RULE-004, fx-derivatives:RULE-005
- Transformations: fx-derivatives:TR-001, fx-derivatives:TR-002, fx-derivatives:TR-003, fx-derivatives:TR-004, fx-derivatives:TR-005, fx-derivatives:TR-006
- Variants: fx-derivatives:VAR-001, fx-derivatives:VAR-002, fx-derivatives:VAR-003
- Enrichments and tentative signals: fx-derivatives:ENR-001, fx-derivatives:ENR-002, fx-derivatives:ENR-003, fx-derivatives:ENR-004, fx-derivatives:ENR-005, fx-derivatives:TENT-001 .. TENT-009

nonBlockingSuggestions: Evidence grounding: Stable rules RULE-004 and RULE-005 each have only 4 supporting examples, and TR-006 has only 2. While these meet the minimum threshold, consider annotating them with a 'thin evidence' marker so agents weigh them more cautiously.

CDM path specificity: Several enrichment and variant entries (ENR-001 through ENR-005, VAR-001 through VAR-003) list 'none recovered' for target CDM paths. Where possible, add at least the expected CDM leaf path (e.g., 'party.partyId.identifier.value' for ENR-001) so agents know where the enrichment would land.

Redundancy/concision: The cookbook contains significant duplication between Stable Rules and Transformations sections (e.g., RULE-002 vs TR-002 for date normalization; RULE-004 vs TR-003 for expiry mapping; RULE-005 vs TR-004 for payment amounts). Consolidating or cross-referencing would reduce length and potential for contradictory guidance.
Redundancy/concision: Enrichment entries ENR-001 and ENR-002 cover the same LEI enrichment phenomenon with nearly identical evidence sets and caveats. Merge into a single entry to reduce noise.

Party-role safety: The cookbook correctly flags buyer/seller inversion (VAR-002, TR-001) and mandates review, which is good. However, the cookbook could be strengthened by explicitly stating that an LLM agent MUST NOT finalize buyer/seller/payer/receiver assignments without human sign-off, rather than only suggesting review.

Exception handling: RULE-004 states 'Do not apply when: Any of expiry date, time, or business center is missing; mark partials for review.' It would be helpful to specify how the agent should represent a partial expiry (e.g., populate what's available and leave others null vs. skip the entire exerciseTerms block).

## Stable Rules

- Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
  - When it applies: FpML contains tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId elements.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value.

  - Do not apply when: tradeId is absent in FpML.
  - Exceptions/notes: Some CDM outputs contain more identifiers than FpML tradeId elements; scheme may differ. Trigger human review in those cases.

- Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate includes a trailing 'Z' (UTC designator).
  - Inspect: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeDate.value (plain ISO date without trailing 'Z').
  - Validate: Confirm only the trailing 'Z' was trimmed; no timezone semantics needed elsewhere.
  - Do not apply when: FpML tradeDate is already a plain date without timezone.

- Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
  - When it applies: FpML includes trade.fxdigitaloption.productType strings.
  - Inspect: trade.fxdigitaloption.productType (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (normalized taxonomy string).
  - Validate: Confirm productType string normalized as observed in evidence; flag if normalization logic is unclear or out of scope.
  - Do not apply when: No productType present.
  - Exceptions/notes: Normalization details are not exhaustively specified; may require analyst review.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: FpML provides expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime and a businessCenter.
  - Inspect: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and related businessCenter fields (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value and exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime and expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: Confirm date, time, and business center are correctly placed. Ensure no timezone semantics are dropped.
  - Do not apply when: Any of expiry date, time, or business center is missing; mark partials for review.

- Payment amounts -> CDM quantities (value + currency unit)
  - When it applies: FpML includes exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Inspect: exchangedCurrency1.paymentAmount and exchangedCurrency2.paymentAmount (amount, currency) (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and trade.tradeLot.quantity.unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm amount and currency are preserved, including sign/scale. If multiple paymentAmount or splitSettlement entries exist, verify any aggregation logic and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: paymentAmount is absent.

## Transformations

- Resolve party hrefs -> CDM party references and roles
  - When it applies: FpML contains partyReference hrefs and buyer/seller or payer/receiver references.

  - Do not apply when: partyReference hrefs are missing or ambiguous.

  - When it applies: FpML tradeHeader.tradeDate includes 'Z'.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.tradeDate.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradedate.value without 'Z'.
  - Validate: Only the trailing 'Z' is removed; no timezone conversion implied.

  - When it applies: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter present in FpML.
  - Inspect: expirydatetime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter.
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value; exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime; expirationTime.businessCenter.value.

  - When it applies: exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount fields present.
  - Inspect: paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value.

  - When it applies: FpML has exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2.
  - Inspect: fxSingleLeg.exchangeRate.rate; exchangeRate.quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2; any quoteBasis context if present.

  - Do not apply when: exchangeRate or quotedCurrencyPair is missing.

  - When it applies: FpML uses splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries.
  - Inspect: splitSettlement blocks and repeated paymentAmount entries.
  - Propose CDM: either a single aggregated trade.tradeLot.quantity or an appropriate set of aggregated quantities per evidence.

  - Do not apply when: Only a single settlement entry exists.

# FPML -> CDM Cookbook: fx-derivatives

## Status

- Operational status: ready
- Agent use policy: Agents may apply these rules during normal FPML to CDM proposal generation.
- Semantic success rate: 100%
- Draft quality: strong
- Draft publication: success

## Trigger Signals

Apply this page when the FpML document includes any of the following top-level sections or product cues:
- fx-derivatives
- FpML sections: header, party, trade
- Trade substructures commonly observed:
  - trade > fxSingleLeg
  - trade > tradeHeader
- Party identifiers and references:
  - party > partyId
  - tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId
- Header metadata:
  - header > conversationId, creationTimestamp, messageId, sendTo, sentBy

## Canonical Mapping Procedure

1. Start from the repeated FpML sections: header, party, trade. [Ensure these sections are present before applying downstream rules.]
2. Map trade identifiers, party references, and trade dates before product-specific economics.
3. Apply recurring mapping rules only when the exact source cues appear in the document (see Stable Rules and Transformations).
4. Apply non-literal transformations (normalizations/reshaping) where indicated by the evidence below.
5. Assemble under CDM scaffolding such as meta and trade, preserving traceability to source identifiers.
6. Treat generated identifiers, global keys, and unmatched party identifiers as enrichments unless the source proves otherwise.

## Stable Rules

- Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
  - When it applies: FpML contains tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId elements.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value.
  - Validate: Verify all FpML tradeId values are preserved in CDM assignedIdentifier.identifier.value. Check for unexpected duplication or scheme differences and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: tradeId is absent in FpML.
  - Exceptions/notes: Some CDM outputs contain more identifiers than FpML tradeId elements; scheme may differ. Trigger human review in those cases.

- Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate includes a trailing 'Z' (UTC designator).
  - Inspect: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeDate.value (plain ISO date without trailing 'Z').
  - Validate: Confirm only the trailing 'Z' was trimmed; no timezone semantics needed elsewhere.
  - Do not apply when: FpML tradeDate is already a plain date without timezone.

- Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
  - When it applies: FpML includes trade.fxdigitaloption.productType strings.
  - Inspect: trade.fxdigitaloption.productType (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (normalized taxonomy string).

# FPML -> CDM Cookbook: fx-derivatives

## Status

- Operational status: ready
- Agent use policy: Agents may apply these rules during normal FPML to CDM proposal generation.
- Semantic success rate: 100%
- Draft quality: strong
- Draft publication: success

## Trigger Signals

Apply this page when the FpML document includes any of the following top-level sections or product cues:
- fx-derivatives
- FpML sections: header, party, trade
- Trade substructures commonly observed:
  - trade > fxSingleLeg
  - trade > tradeHeader
- Party identifiers and references:
  - party > partyId
  - tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId
- Header metadata:
  - header > conversationId, creationTimestamp, messageId, sendTo, sentBy

## Canonical Mapping Procedure

1. Start from the repeated FpML sections: header, party, trade. [Ensure these sections are present before applying downstream rules.]
2. Map trade identifiers, party references, and trade dates before product-specific economics.
3. Apply recurring mapping rules only when the exact source cues appear in the document (see Stable Rules and Transformations).
4. Apply non-literal transformations (normalizations/reshaping) where indicated by the evidence below.
5. Assemble under CDM scaffolding such as meta and trade, preserving traceability to source identifiers.
6. Treat generated identifiers, global keys, and unmatched party identifiers as enrichments unless the source proves otherwise.

## Stable Rules

- Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
  - When it applies: FpML contains tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId elements.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value.
  - Validate: Verify all FpML tradeId values are preserved in CDM assignedIdentifier.identifier.value. Check for unexpected duplication or scheme differences and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: tradeId is absent in FpML.
  - Exceptions/notes: Some CDM outputs contain more identifiers than FpML tradeId elements; scheme may differ. Trigger human review in those cases.

- Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate includes a trailing 'Z' (UTC designator).
  - Inspect: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeDate.value (plain ISO date without trailing 'Z').
  - Validate: Confirm only the trailing 'Z' was trimmed; no timezone semantics needed elsewhere.
  - Do not apply when: FpML tradeDate is already a plain date without timezone.

- Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
  - When it applies: FpML includes trade.fxdigitaloption.productType strings.
  - Inspect: trade.fxdigitaloption.productType (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (normalized taxonomy string).
  - Validate: Confirm productType string normalized as observed in evidence; flag if normalization logic is unclear or out of scope.
  - Do not apply when: No productType present.
  - Exceptions/notes: Normalization details are not exhaustively specified; may require analyst review.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: FpML provides expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime and a businessCenter.
  - Inspect: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and related businessCenter fields (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value and exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime and expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: Confirm date, time, and business center are correctly placed. Ensure no timezone semantics are dropped.
  - Do not apply when: Any of expiry date, time, or business center is missing; mark partials for review.

- Payment amounts -> CDM quantities (value + currency unit)
  - When it applies: FpML includes exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Inspect: exchangedCurrency1.paymentAmount and exchangedCurrency2.paymentAmount (amount, currency) (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and trade.tradeLot.quantity.unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm amount and currency are preserved, including sign/scale. If multiple paymentAmount or splitSettlement entries exist, verify any aggregation logic and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: paymentAmount is absent.

## Transformations

- Resolve party hrefs -> CDM party references and roles
  - When it applies: FpML contains partyReference hrefs and buyer/seller or payer/receiver references.
  - Inspect: partyReference hrefs in buyer/seller and payer/receiver contexts (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: party references with roles (e.g., Party1/Party2) used in buyerSeller and payout sections.
  - Validate: Cross-check Party1/Party2 and payer/receiver with FpML references; flag any polarity inversions for analyst review.
  - Do not apply when: partyReference hrefs are missing or ambiguous.
  - Exceptions/notes: Evidence shows possible inversions of roles; treat polarity as tentative and review-critical.

- Date normalization (trim trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML tradeHeader.tradeDate includes 'Z'.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.tradeDate.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradedate.value without 'Z'.
  - Validate: Only the trailing 'Z' is removed; no timezone conversion implied.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter present in FpML.
  - Inspect: expirydatetime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter.
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value; exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime; expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: All three components preserved.

- PaymentAmount -> Quantity mapping
  - When it applies: exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount fields present.
  - Inspect: paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Preserve amount, currency, sign, and scale. For multiple entries, confirm aggregation or separate entries per evidence and flag if unclear.

- ExchangeRate + quoted pair -> Price assembly
  - When it applies: FpML has exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2.
  - Inspect: fxSingleLeg.exchangeRate.rate; exchangeRate.quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2; any quoteBasis context if present.
  - Propose CDM: price.value.value, price.unit.currency.value, price.perUnitOf.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm price numeric value and currency unit/perUnitOf assigned per the quotedCurrencyPair; flag if quoteBasis/strikeQuoteBasis interpretation is needed and not explicit.
  - Do not apply when: exchangeRate or quotedCurrencyPair is missing.

- Split/Multiple settlement entries -> aggregated quantity
  - When it applies: FpML uses splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries.
  - Inspect: splitSettlement blocks and repeated paymentAmount entries.
  - Propose CDM: either a single aggregated trade.tradeLot.quantity or an appropriate set of aggregated quantities per evidence.
  - Validate: Confirm aggregation approach (sums, ordering, rounding) is consistent with evidence or business rules; otherwise flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: Only a single settlement entry exists.

- Tentative: Normalize trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate -> trade.tradeDate.value
  - Apply only when exact match to the observed pattern; mark for analyst review.

## Variants And Branches

- AssignedIdentifier.scheme differences
  - Signal: Scheme in CDM may differ from FpML tradeIdScheme (or absence thereof).
  - Action: Do not copy scheme verbatim; treat as potential normalization/override. Flag for analyst review.

- Buyer/Seller role inversion
  - Signal: CDM buyer/seller or payer/receiver roles may appear inverted relative to FpML hrefs.
  - Action: Treat role polarity as tentative; require analyst validation of Party1/Party2 mapping.

- Duplicated tradeIdentifier entries
  - Signal: CDM may contain more tradeIdentifier entries than FpML tradeId elements.
  - Action: Do not assume 1:1 mapping; flag duplicates/additional identifiers for review.

## Enrichment And Defaults

- Generated/default party identifiers under partyid.identifier.value
  - Signal: CDM often includes LEI-like or generated party identifiers not present in FpML.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; do not generate unless approved. Flag for review.

- Party LEI or generated identifiers inserted
  - Signal: LEI-like identifiers appear in CDM without FpML source.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; confirm source/approval before populating.

- Metadata taxonomy scheme enrichment under name.meta.scheme
  - Signal: CDM includes taxonomy scheme metadata even when FpML lacks a scheme.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; do not insert without approved default. Flag for review.

- Product type normalization -> taxonomy name and meta.scheme enrichment
  - Signal: Normalized product names and added taxonomy scheme metadata observed.
  - Action: Treat scheme insertion as enrichment; normalization should be limited to evidence-backed patterns; flag for review.

- Taxonomy scheme metadata added under name.meta.scheme
  - Signal: Scheme metadata present in CDM without explicit FpML value.
  - Action: Treat as enrichment; verify choice of scheme externally.

## Human Review Triggers

- Source for any LEI or generated party identifiers is absent in FpML; confirm provenance before including.
- Buyer/seller or payer/receiver polarity appears inverted relative to FpML hrefs.
- Unclear derivation of CDM Party1/Party2 labels from FpML party references.
- Duplicated or augmented tradeIdentifier entries relative to FpML tradeId.
- Multiple splitSettlement/paymentAmount entries: confirm aggregation vs separation.
- Differences in assignedIdentifier.scheme vs FpML tradeId scheme: confirm normalization.
- Mapping of exchangedCurrency leg to SettlementPayout payerReceiver is unclear.
- Any tentative pattern applied (date normalization; expiry mapping; price assembly) without explicit cues.

## Validation Checklist

- Identify FpML tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId and confirm CDM trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value preserves each value.
- Check tradeHeader.tradeDate for trailing 'Z'; ensure CDM trade.tradeDate.value trims 'Z'.
- For options, confirm trade.fxdigitaloption.productType is mapped to trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value with expected normalization.
- Confirm expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and businessCenter map to adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value, exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime, and expirationTime.businessCenter.value respectively.
- Verify exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency map to trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value; preserve amount, currency, sign, and scale.
- Resolve partyReference hrefs; verify Party1/Party2 and payer/receiver direction against FpML context.
- When exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2 exist, assemble CDM price.value.value, price.unit.currency.value, price.perUnitOf.currency.value; confirm any quoteBasis interpretation or flag for review.
- If splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries exist, validate aggregation or separation per evidence; flag if logic is unclear.
- Confirm every enriched/defaulted CDM value is either present in FpML or explicitly approved as a default.
- Ensure each populated CDM field in the proposal cites an applicable cookbook rule id or is marked as an assumption.

## Do Not Assume

- Do not treat Generated/default party identifiers appear under partyid.identifier.value as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Party LEI or generated identifiers inserted as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Metadata taxonomy scheme enrichment under name.meta.scheme as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Product type normalization -> taxonomy name and meta.scheme enrichment as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Do not treat Taxonomy scheme metadata added under name.meta.scheme as a guaranteed direct mapping rule yet.
- Source of party LEI values missing in FpML.
- Do not infer Party1/Party2, buyer/seller, or payer/receiver direction from document order alone.
- Do not invent identifiers, global keys, external keys, or LEIs when they are not source-backed.
- Do not guess normalized exchange, taxonomy, or scheme values without a controlled mapping or evidence.
- Do not apply tentative patterns without matching source evidence.
- Do not invent enriched identifiers, global keys, exchange codes, or defaults without source-backed evidence.
- Do not treat caveated or unclear behavior as a stable mapping rule.
- Do not treat as stable: Derivation of CDM party role labels (Party1/Party2) from FpML party hrefs.
- Do not treat as stable: Source and reliability of party LEI or generated identifiers included in CDM.
- Do not treat as stable: Rules that create additional or duplicate tradeIdentifier entries in CDM.
- Do not treat as stable: Precise aggregation rules used when merging splitSettlement/multiple paymentAmount entries.

  - Signals: header, trade, party.
  - Guidance: exchange rate copied; payment amounts to quantities; tradeIds copied; strip trailing 'Z' from dates.
  - Validate: Review party LEI source; verify payer/receiver roles.

# FPML -> CDM Cookbook: fx-derivatives

## Status

- Operational status: ready
- Agent use policy: Agents may apply these rules during normal FPML to CDM proposal generation.
- Semantic success rate: 100%
- Draft quality: strong
- Draft publication: success

## Trigger Signals

Apply this page when the FpML document includes any of the following top-level sections or product cues:
- fx-derivatives
- FpML sections: header, party, trade
- Trade substructures commonly observed:
  - trade > fxSingleLeg
  - trade > tradeHeader
- Party identifiers and references:
  - party > partyId
  - tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId
- Header metadata:
  - header > conversationId, creationTimestamp, messageId, sendTo, sentBy

## Canonical Mapping Procedure

1. Start from the repeated FpML sections: header, party, trade. [Ensure these sections are present before applying downstream rules.]
2. Map trade identifiers, party references, and trade dates before product-specific economics.
3. Apply recurring mapping rules only when the exact source cues appear in the document (see Stable Rules and Transformations).
4. Apply non-literal transformations (normalizations/reshaping) where indicated by the evidence below.
5. Assemble under CDM scaffolding such as meta and trade, preserving traceability to source identifiers.
6. Treat generated identifiers, global keys, and unmatched party identifiers as enrichments unless the source proves otherwise.

## Stable Rules

- Trade identifier -> assignedIdentifier.value
  - When it applies: FpML contains tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId elements.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.partyTradeIdentifier.tradeId (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier.identifier.value.
  - Validate: Verify all FpML tradeId values are preserved in CDM assignedIdentifier.identifier.value. Check for unexpected duplication or scheme differences and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: tradeId is absent in FpML.
  - Exceptions/notes: Some CDM outputs contain more identifiers than FpML tradeId elements; scheme may differ. Trigger human review in those cases.

- Trade date normalization (remove trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate includes a trailing 'Z' (UTC designator).
  - Inspect: trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeDate.value (plain ISO date without trailing 'Z').
  - Validate: Confirm only the trailing 'Z' was trimmed; no timezone semantics needed elsewhere.
  - Do not apply when: FpML tradeDate is already a plain date without timezone.

- Option product type -> CDM taxonomy name
  - When it applies: FpML includes trade.fxdigitaloption.productType strings.
  - Inspect: trade.fxdigitaloption.productType (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.product.taxonomyName.value or value.name.value (normalized taxonomy string).
  - Validate: Confirm productType string normalized as observed in evidence; flag if normalization logic is unclear or out of scope.
  - Do not apply when: No productType present.
  - Exceptions/notes: Normalization details are not exhaustively specified; may require analyst review.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: FpML provides expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime and a businessCenter.
  - Inspect: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, and related businessCenter fields (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value and exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime and expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: Confirm date, time, and business center are correctly placed. Ensure no timezone semantics are dropped.
  - Do not apply when: Any of expiry date, time, or business center is missing; mark partials for review.

- Payment amounts -> CDM quantities (value + currency unit)
  - When it applies: FpML includes exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Inspect: exchangedCurrency1.paymentAmount and exchangedCurrency2.paymentAmount (amount, currency) (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and trade.tradeLot.quantity.unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm amount and currency are preserved, including sign/scale. If multiple paymentAmount or splitSettlement entries exist, verify any aggregation logic and flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: paymentAmount is absent.

## Transformations

- Resolve party hrefs -> CDM party references and roles
  - When it applies: FpML contains partyReference hrefs and buyer/seller or payer/receiver references.
  - Inspect: partyReference hrefs in buyer/seller and payer/receiver contexts (FpML).
  - Propose CDM: party references with roles (e.g., Party1/Party2) used in buyerSeller and payout sections.
  - Validate: Cross-check Party1/Party2 and payer/receiver with FpML references; flag any polarity inversions for analyst review.
  - Do not apply when: partyReference hrefs are missing or ambiguous.
  - Exceptions/notes: Evidence shows possible inversions of roles; treat polarity as tentative and review-critical.

- Date normalization (trim trailing 'Z')
  - When it applies: FpML tradeHeader.tradeDate includes 'Z'.
  - Inspect: tradeHeader.tradeDate.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradedate.value without 'Z'.
  - Validate: Only the trailing 'Z' is removed; no timezone conversion implied.

- Expiry date/time/businessCenter -> exerciseTerms.expiration
  - When it applies: expiryDateTime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter present in FpML.
  - Inspect: expirydatetime.expiryDate, expiryTime, businessCenter.
  - Propose CDM: adjustableDate.adjustedDate.value; exerciseTerms.expirationTime.hourMinuteTime; expirationTime.businessCenter.value.
  - Validate: All three components preserved.

- PaymentAmount -> Quantity mapping
  - When it applies: exchangedCurrencyX.paymentAmount fields present.
  - Inspect: paymentAmount.amount and .currency.
  - Propose CDM: trade.tradeLot.quantity.value and .unit.currency.value.
  - Validate: Preserve amount, currency, sign, and scale. For multiple entries, confirm aggregation or separate entries per evidence and flag if unclear.

- ExchangeRate + quoted pair -> Price assembly
  - When it applies: FpML has exchangeRate.rate and quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2.
  - Inspect: fxSingleLeg.exchangeRate.rate; exchangeRate.quotedCurrencyPair.currency1/currency2; any quoteBasis context if present.
  - Propose CDM: price.value.value, price.unit.currency.value, price.perUnitOf.currency.value.
  - Validate: Confirm price numeric value and currency unit/perUnitOf assigned per the quotedCurrencyPair; flag if quoteBasis/strikeQuoteBasis interpretation is needed and not explicit.
  - Do not apply when: exchangeRate or quotedCurrencyPair is missing.

- Split/Multiple settlement entries -> aggregated quantity
  - When it applies: FpML uses splitSettlement or multiple paymentAmount entries.
  - Inspect: splitSettlement blocks and repeated paymentAmount entries.
  - Propose CDM: either a single aggregated trade.tradeLot.quantity or an appropriate set of aggregated quantities per evidence.
  - Validate: Confirm aggregation approach (sums, ordering, rounding) is consistent with evidence or business rules; otherwise flag for review.
  - Do not apply when: Only a single settlement entry exists.

- Tentative: Normalize trade.tradeHeader.tradeDate -> trade.tradeDate.value
  - Apply only when exact match to the observed pattern; mark for analyst review.
